title: Filtering the employees table by numbers · part 5

steps.title: Filter then sort: salary < 14500.0
steps.prompt:
Filter first, then ORDER BY tidies what is left.
LIMIT 3 keeps the top of that sorted list.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary < 14500.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM employees.
Add WHERE salary < 14500.0.
Add ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3.
Write: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary < 14500.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary < 14500.0 ORDER BY salary LIMIT 3;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE trims, ORDER BY sorts, LIMIT cuts.

steps.title: Keep salary <= 14500.0
steps.prompt:
Numbers compare with small symbols:
  > bigger   < smaller   = exactly   != not equal
Keep the rows where salary is at most 14500.0.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary <= 14500.0;
hints: Start with SELECT id FROM employees.
Add WHERE after the table name.
The test is salary <= 14500.0.
Write: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary <= 14500.0;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT id FROM employees WHERE salary <= 14500.0;
steps.memory_trick: WHERE keeps only the rows that pass the test.

steps.title: Count rows salary <= 14500.0
steps.prompt: COUNT(*) counts how many rows survive the filter.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT count(*) FROM employees WHERE salary <= 14500.0;
